confidences.reason: Sound. The log shows the plan required checking whether each member held a C‑suite role at the time they joined Apple’s board. At Step 7, the agent concluded for Arthur D. Levinson that because he had been CEO, he “held a C‑suite position before joining Apple’s Board,” shifting the criterion from “at the time of joining” to “ever held before joining.” This phrasing and standard are then repeated for all subsequent members, culminating in the incorrect global conclusion that none joined without a C‑suite role. Although Levinson did in fact hold a C‑suite role at the time he joined, Step 7 is where the methodological misinterpretation first appears and drives the later incorrect outcome, and it was never corrected thereafter.

The log supports that this is the earliest point where the incorrect criterion was introduced and applied.

Wagner) continued to apply the same flawed ‘before joining’ criterion and never corrected it to ‘at the time of joining.’ The final conclusions similarly relied on this incorrect temporal assumption.
